body: Bones support the body, protect some organs and provide surfaces on which muscles can act. A joint is where bones meet. Some joints allow a large range of motion, while others allow very little. Tendons transmit force from muscles to bones. At the elbow, muscle force can bend or straighten the arm.

Skeletal muscle can shorten as its fibers generate tension. Motion usually involves several muscles and coordinated signals from the nervous system. The pottery photograph shows one activity in which the hand's joints, muscles and sense of touch work together.

limitations: An articulated museum skeleton shows the arrangement of bones. It omits living tissue and some features that vary with age, development, disability and individual anatomy.
purpose: Explain how bones, muscles and joints transfer force during movement.
